findings.title: String timestamps silently defeat newest-first workflow ordering
findings.where: scripts/read-workflows.mjs:119 accepts startTime through boundedScalar; scripts/read-workflows.mjs:144 subtracts startTime values; scripts/read-workflows.mjs:157 applies that comparator.
findings.what: boundedScalar preserves arbitrary strings, but subtracting an ISO timestamp or other nonnumeric string yields NaN. Array.sort then treats the comparison as no ordering, so the documented newest-first result can remain in directory iteration order and downstream workflow-health consumers receive stale or misranked runs.
findings.fix: Normalize startTime to a finite numeric epoch during projection, parsing supported timestamp strings explicitly or replacing invalid values with null; make the comparator operate only on normalized numbers.
findings.acceptance: Add fixtures written in reverse chronological discovery order with numeric, supported string, and invalid startTime values; assert both readWorkflows and readWorkflowsSync return valid runs newest-first and handle invalid timestamps deterministically.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the same unvalidated boundedScalar result flows directly from trimWorkflowRun into numeric subtraction with no intervening timestamp normalization.

findings.title: Per-directory discovery caps permit multiplicative filesystem traversal
findings.where: scripts/read-workflows.mjs:166 derives one directory-entry cap from the run cap; the async walk applies it separately at lines 311, 335, and 344, mirrored synchronously at lines 379, 403, and 412.
findings.what: The nominal 50,000-run bound is not a global work bound. Up to 50,001 projects can each trigger scans of up to 50,001 sessions, even when none contains a manifest, and each qualifying session can add another capped workflow-directory scan. The server route and synchronous ingest path can therefore suffer extreme latency or blocking despite returning zero runs.
findings.fix: Track one shared discovery budget across the complete traversal, decrement it for every examined directory entry, and stop with truncated=true when exhausted; use a separate, substantially smaller configurable discovery budget if needed.
findings.acceptance: Create a sparse nested fixture whose total entries exceed a small injected global discovery budget without producing runs; assert async and sync readers stop at that total budget, return truncated=true, and do not continue scanning later directories.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read of both implementations confirmed every readDirentsBounded call receives a fresh default counter and only runs.length can terminate the outer traversal; no aggregate discovery counter exists.
